documents.abstract: Abstract The global adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in journalism has increasingly, offering benefits such as enhanced efficiency, accuracy, and the ability to process large volumes of data swiftly. Despite these advantages, there is a gap in research regarding how journalism students, who represent the future of the industry, perceive the integration of AI in news writing. The focus of this study is to examine the level of awareness of AI tools among journalism students, identify the benefits and the perceived challenges that could be attached to its adoption in news writing. The study adopted a survey technique and sampled 324 students of the Federal Polytechnic, Nasarawa. The findings show that Journalism students are aware of the existence of AI tools that can be adopted for news writing and the perceived benefits are more useful in writing precision and other scientific reports. The finding underscores the benefits of AI tools in the advancement of writing styles among journalism students. However, ethical concerns, high cost and restrictive accessibility to some of the tools are parts of the barriers affecting the use of the tools. It therefore suggests that, journalism institutions should incorporate ethical use and guides into their curriculum in order prepare students for the future on the use of AI tools that are directly related to journalism practices Key Words: Awareness, Attitudes, Perceptions, Artificial Intelligence, News Writing

Los modelos de lenguaje se usan para evaluar respuestas abiertas, y sus resultados suelen resumirse en una cifra de acuerdo con personas o en un puesto de clasificación. Este artículo sintetiza once fuentes primarias y separa tres cosas que esas cifras mezclan: la métrica de acuerdo (porcentaje de coincidencia, kappa de Cohen o correlación entre rankings) y la población sobre la que se calcula; los sesgos medidos (posición, longitud o verbosidad, estilo y autopreferencia) y su tamaño en cada montaje; y el protocolo (comparación por pares o puntuación absoluta, con o sin referencia, con o sin intercambio de posiciones). En MT-Bench, el acuerdo entre GPT-4 y expertos es del 85 % cuando se excluyen los empates y del 66 % cuando se incluyen; el acuerdo entre expertos baja de forma paralela. La consistencia ante el intercambio de posición varía entre el 23,8 % y el 65,0 % según el juez en un conjunto de pares casi equivalentes, y cae cuando la diferencia de calidad es pequeña. Preferir texto propio tampoco equivale a favoritismo: en tareas con clave, la preferencia propia de los modelos fuertes coincide mayoritariamente con la respuesta correcta. Ninguna de estas magnitudes se presenta como propiedad general del juez ni se compara en una escala común. Se propone un protocolo de validación local, sin validación experimental, que fija la decisión, la población, la referencia, los empates, los controles y la incertidumbre. No se presentan experimentos nuevos ni un metaanálisis. English abstract: Language models are used to evaluate open-ended responses, and their results are often summarised as a single human-agreement figure or a leaderboard rank. This paper synthesises eleven primary sources and separates three things those figures conflate: the agreement metric (percentage agreement, Cohen's kappa or rank correlation) and the population it is computed on; measured biases (position, length or verbosity, style and self-preference) and their size in each setup; and the protocol (pairwise comparison or absolute scoring, with or without a reference, with or without position swapping). On MT-Bench, GPT-4–expert agreement is 85% when ties are excluded and 66% when they are included; expert–expert agreement falls in parallel. Consistency under position swapping ranges from 23.8% to 65.0% across judges on a set of near-equivalent pairs, and drops when the quality gap is small. Preferring one's own text is not favouritism by itself either: on tasks with a key, the self-preference of strong models mostly coincides with the correct answer. None of these magnitudes is presented as a general property of the judge or compared on a common scale. A local validation protocol, without experimental validation, is proposed that fixes the decision, population, reference, ties, controls and uncertainty. No new experiments or meta-analysis are reported. Working paper de la serie WHITE-PAPERS (wp-2026-032, v0.9). Incluye versión en español e inglés. No revisado por pares. Uso de herramientas de IA declarado en el manuscrito; sin conflictos de interés ni financiación.

Trajectory transfer from rollout to training affects both learning quality and system efficiency in large language model reinforcement learning (RL). Enforcing batch-wide training requirements can delay the admission of completed trajectories, resulting in higher architectural staleness: the additional parameter-version gap from disaggregated pipelining relative to colocated execution. Beyond admission, misalignment between data access and training consumption causes redundant movement and unnecessary waiting when transferring large trajectory payloads. We present KnitTrans, a system that coordinates the rollout-to-training path through three designs. First, constraint-preserving mini-batch admission allows flexibility in early mini-batch composition, while checking that enough capacity remains to satisfy the remaining quotas. Second, on-demand trajectory data access matches storage units to consumer assignments and overlaps micro-batch data preparation with computation. Third, multimodal encoding deduplication supports reuse across a mini-batch while preserving gradient contributions from all backbone micro-batches. Experiments show up to 93% lower architectural staleness than with train-batch admission, narrowing the learning-quality gap between disaggregated execution and colocated execution. On multimodal workloads, KnitTrans reduces transfer latency by two orders of magnitude and achieves a speedup of up to 5.8 times in transfer plus training over the baseline.

Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly impacted various fields, including medicine. As AI integration in medicine expands, medical students and professionals need to develop a comprehensive understanding of its applications. This study aimed to explore the self-reported knowledge and attitudes of undergraduate Egyptian medical students regarding artificial intelligence application in medical practice. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted between June and August 2025 among undergraduate medical students from seven Egyptian medical schools. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Data were collected via a validated structured web-based questionnaire distributed through social media to assess students’ demographics, knowledge, and attitudes toward AI applications in medical practice. This study included 1438 medical students with a mean age of 20.3 years ± 1.9 years. Overall, 55.3% demonstrated good knowledge and 66.8% showed a positive attitude toward AI applications in medical practice. Good knowledge was significantly higher among students in higher academic years (3rd year AOR = 1.88, P = 0.006; 4th year AOR = 2.02, P = 0.007; 5th year AOR = 1.86, P = 0.034) and among those reporting peers and mentors (AOR = 1.35, P = 0.017), scientific papers and books (AOR = 1.71, P < 0.001), training courses (AOR = 1.43, P = 0.004), and mass media (AOR = 1.32, P = 0.036) as their main sources of AI information. A positive attitude toward AI was significantly more common among male students (AOR = 1.50, P = 0.001), 4th-year students (AOR = 1.97, P = 0.014), and those willing to enroll in an AI course (AOR = 1.30, P = 0.039). YouTube was perceived as the most valuable social media source for AI-related information (90.4%), followed by Telegram (86.6%) and WhatsApp (65.2%). Although the Egyptian medical students who participated in this study demonstrated generally positive attitudes toward AI and a willingness to learn, they may be navigating this transition with limited institutional guidance. These findings suggest that medical schools should consider integrating AI-related technical literacy and ethical reasoning into the core curriculum.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Advancements in large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for automating challenging and time-intensive Knowledge Engineering (KE) tasks. Constructing an ontology is particularly complex when modeling logical axioms, especially among novice knowledge engineers and domain experts with limited KE training. Consequently, ontologies often contain modeling errors, undermining ontology-based applications and hindering subsequent KE tasks. Thus, it is important to investigate how LLMs can support KE tasks such as the evaluation of ontologies. However, systematically evaluating LLM performance remains challenging due to a lack of comprehensive, task-specific benchmarks needed for such LLM capability assessments. As a result, selecting the right LLM to support knowledge engineers is nontrivial. This study investigates how LLMs can support four concrete ontology evaluation subtasks: detection, classification, explanation, and possible correction of modeling issues, focusing on the use of existential, universal, and cardinality property restrictions. We construct a benchmark of student-built ontologies and assess the performance of four LLMs—GPT-4o, ClaudeSonnet, DeepSeekV3, and Llama3.3—on these KE subtasks. Additionally, we exemplify an annotation framework for qualitatively evaluating LLM outputs and analyse the capabilities of each model. Our findings reveal differences in model behavior and task-specific strengths, underscoring the importance of selecting an appropriate model for each KE task.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Les entreprises intègrent progressivement des outils d’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans leurs activités de prévision financière, mais les travaux consacrés au contexte marocain portent surtout sur la performance prédictive des modèles et peu sur la manière dont la prévision est mobilisée dans la décision. Cette étude comble ce vide en examinant si l’usage de l’IA dans la prévision financière et la qualité des données sont associés à la qualité perçue des prévisions, et si celle-ci est associée à la qualité de la décision stratégique. Elle contribue à la littérature en spécifiant la qualité perçue des prévisions comme mécanisme statistique de transmission entre l’usage de l’IA et la décision. Le design est mixte imbriqué, à dominante quantitative : dix entretiens exploratoires apportent un cadrage contextuel, puis une enquête non probabiliste auprès de 250 professionnels de la finance et du pilotage d’entreprises marocaines est analysée par PLS-SEM. Les résultats indiquent des associations positives, de force modérée à faible : la qualité des données (β = 0,259) et, davantage, l’usage de l’IA (β = 0,364) sont associés à la qualité perçue des prévisions (R2 = 0,250), elle-même associée à la qualité décisionnelle (β = 0,334 ; R2 = 0,207). L’effet indirect de l’usage de l’IA sur la décision est significatif (β = 0,121), à côté d’un effet direct (β = 0,197), ce qui correspond à une médiation statistique partielle complémentaire. Les entretiens et la question ouverte soulignent la gouvernance des données, la supervision humaine et l’accompagnement des utilisateurs, sans que le modèle les teste. Le plan transversal, la mesure perceptuelle et la validation incomplète des items appellent à la prudence dans l’interprétation. As finance functions digitalize, firms increasingly integrate artificial intelligence (AI) tools into forecasting, yet research on Morocco has mainly examined the predictive performance of models and says little about how forecasts are used in decisions. This study addresses this gap by examining whether AI use in financial forecasting and data quality are associated with perceived forecast quality, and whether the latter is associated with strategic decision quality. It contributes by specifying perceived forecast quality as a statistical transmission mechanism between AI use and decision quality. The study adopts an embedded mixed-methods design with quantitative dominance: ten exploratory interviews provide contextual framing, followed by a non-probability survey of 250 finance and management-control professionals in Moroccan firms, analyzed with PLS-SEM. Results show positive associations of moderate to small magnitude: data quality (β = 0.259) and, to a greater extent, AI use (β = 0.364) are associated with perceived forecast quality (R2 = 0.250), which is in turn associated with decision quality (β = 0.334; R2 = 0.207). The indirect effect of AI use on decision quality is significant (β = 0.121; 95% CI [0.070, 0.183]) alongside a significant direct effect (β = 0.197), indicating complementary partial statistical mediation. Interviews and an open-ended question point to data governance, human oversight, and user support as enabling conditions, which the model does not test. The study thus shifts attention from algorithmic performance alone to the organizational appropriation of AI-assisted forecasting. The cross-sectional design, the perceptual measurement of forecast quality, and the incomplete validation of the items call for caution in interpreting the findings.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based analysis of intraoperative laparoscopic videos has the potential to improve surgical decision-making and precision. However, effective surgical assistance requires models that can generalize across diverse intraoperative tasks. Here we present LapaFM, a foundation model for laparoscopic surgery trained on more than 20,000 minutes of surgical videos using a multi-stage continual learning strategy that mitigates catastrophic forgetting and inter-task interference. LapaFM learns multimodal visual representations and supports multiple tasks, including smoke removal, surgical phase recognition, instrument and polyp segmentation, and lesion identification. The model was evaluated on 13 retrospective and two prospective cohorts collected from different imaging devices. LapaFM consistently outperformed task-specific models and existing foundation models across datasets, and also generalized to gastrointestinal endoscopy tasks, including polyp detection and classification. Notably, it recovered over 90% of smoke-obscured frames and achieved clinician-level or superior performance in lymph node metastasis prediction and prospective polyp classification.

Abstract As active distribution networks (ADNs) become increasingly saturated with intermittent renewable energy sources, maintaining voltage within safe operational limits has become a critical and complex task, requiring advanced control methods beyond traditional rule‐based approaches. This paper proposes a novel voltage control framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with the soft actor‐critic (SAC) algorithm to enhance the performance of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in ADNs. The core idea is to leverage the LLM as an external knowledge source during the early stage of training to generate highly interpretable and physically meaningful control action suggestions for key voltage regulation devices. A dynamic action fusion mechanism is designed to combine the LLM‐guided actions with SAC policy outputs. As training progresses, the influence of the LLM gradually diminishes, ultimately yielding a fully autonomous SAC policy. Tests on modified IEEE 33‐ and 123‐bus distribution systems show that the proposed method outperforms the standard SAC in terms of convergence efficiency, voltage deviation reduction and control stability. It effectively mitigates policy oscillations during the early exploration phase and significantly reduces the switching frequency of mechanical devices under the learned policy, thereby contributing to longer equipment service life and higher operational reliability.

Large language models such as GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, and BioMedLM are being increasingly applied to clinical decision support tasks including diagnostic reasoning, clinical documentation, medical question answering, and patient-facing health communication, with several studies reporting performance comparable to trained clinicians on structured benchmarks. However, the current pace of adoption has outrun the critical evaluation of whether these models are genuinely safe, equitable, and sustainable for deployment in real-world healthcare environments. This narrative review argues that the existing literature has focused disproportionately on benchmark performance while giving insufficient attention to the conditions required for these models to function as trustworthy long-term clinical tools. Drawing on published evidence across medical informatics, clinical artificial intelligence, and natural language processing, we synthesise model performance across four clinical task areas and examine documented limitations including factual hallucination, demographic bias, and poor generalisability outside controlled settings that are already present in current deployments. We further identify five structural sustainability challenges that obstruct responsible deployment at scale, and propose a corresponding five-pillar framework alongside a priority research agenda for closing the gaps this review identifies. This review contributes a critically grounded perspective to the growing discourse on artificial intelligence for sustainable healthcare, with direct relevance to Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and Sustainable Development Goal 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and offers concrete guidance for developing clinical models that are safe, inclusive, and viable across diverse global health contexts.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformer models performed poorly overall. Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.

AI coding agents are increasingly integrated into software development workflows. However, most coding agent studies rely on benchmarks similar to SWE-bench, which assume autonomous agents operating in a single trajectory. This assumption does not mirror real-world usage, where developers interactively collaborate with agents. We address this gap by studying human-in-the-loop agent trajectories in the wild, focusing on 7,581 Copilot-authored PRs with publicly accessible session data. We find that 58% of Copilot PRs have no human intervention, and that when developers do intervene, collaboration is brief (median of 2 Human-AI loops). Merged PRs also tend to have fewer initial trajectory iterations than unmerged ones. We also find that the trajectory following the first human intervention exhibits a significant drop of 20.8 iterations and 8.4 min in duration. However, trajectories following later interventions show minimal iteration drops and no significant duration change, signifying that most of the work happens in the initial trajectory. Our qualitative analysis of illustrative PRs explains this pattern: many developer interventions are small, focused requests that Copilot completes in shorter later trajectories. We also illustrate that developers collaborate with Copilot in multiple ways, including delegated work through feedback as well as adding their own commits. However, we find that developers may need to guide Copilot through multiple (sometimes repeated) interventions in the PR, or even across multiple editions of the PR.

In the modern world, where digital technology plays an important role in people’s lives, artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain technologies have been the major catalysts of innovation and socio-economic development. However, this rapid evolution of technology has been causing challenges to well-established legal systems. This study examines the current issues of the legal regulation of AI and blockchain technologies within both national and international contexts. This paper explores the attempts of governments and international organisations to create flexible and adaptive legal regulations that keep pace with the rapid progress of technologies and at the same time protect human rights and privacy. Ethical dilemmas, responsibility mechanisms and the importance of clarity in AI decisions are given special attention. Moreover, the study analyses the legal consequences of smart contracts, decentralised autonomous organisations (DAOs) and the way data is processed by AI within blockchain environments. The research highlights the international tendency towards convergence of digital laws by comparing legal approaches in different regions such as the European Union, the United States, South Korea, Kazakhstan, and other countries. The study proposes a comparative accountability-oriented framework for AI and blockchain governance, focusing on legal certainty, data protection, human oversight, innovation support, and cross-border interoperability.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping the landscape of organizational leadership, with travel management systems (TMS) emerging as a critical arena for this transformation. This chapter examines how contemporary leaders can effectively drive AI-enabled change within corporate travel ecosystems. Drawing on established leadership theory, organizational change models, and emerging empirical evidence, it explores the strategic competencies required to navigate the convergence of AI and travel operations. The chapter addresses the ethical dimensions of algorithmic decision-making, workforce adaptation challenges, and the imperative for data governance. Case-based insights illuminate how visionary leadership accelerates TMS modernization. Findings suggest that successful AI integration demands not only technological acumen but also emotional intelligence, change management expertise, and a commitment to inclusive innovation. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking framework for AI-ready leadership in travel management contexts.

documents.abstract: Abstract The development and ubiquitous availability of large language model based systems (LLMs) poses a plurality of potentials and risks for education in schools and universities. In this paper, we provide an analysis and discussion of the overreliance concern as one specific risk: that students might fail to acquire important skills, or be inhibited in the acquisition of these skills, because they overly rely on LLMs. We use the distinction between local and global goals of education to guide our investigation. In our view, the harm of LLM overreliance is specifically that it severs the connection between local educational goals (e.g., successfully solving a specific kind of math problem) and global educational goals (e.g., acquiring general skills for mathematics). Based on this analysis, we sketch three possible responses to the overreliance concern: preserving both local and global goals while making minimal changes to educational practice (a conservative approach), changing global and local educational goals (a revisionary perspective), and preserving global educational goals while changing local goals (an in-between view). Since different types of responses have different benefits and weaknesses, we think that it is likely that an optimal response ultimately combines elements from all three types.

Cancer is a major global health issue with rising incidence and mortality. Early detection, tumor characterization, and disease surveillance are crucial for timely, effective treatment and ultimately reduce mortality. Liquid biopsy (LB) has emerged as a valuable detection tool, offering a non-invasive method to detect tumor-derived biomarkers in body fluids and demonstrating translational potential. To increase biomarker sensitivity, high-throughput sequencing platforms deliver massive volumes of data. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is pivotal to enabling large-scale, complex data integration. This contribution assesses the current state of integrative AI-based research in the LB field and provides methodological guidance. First, we conducted a PubMed search and found that the literature is sparse in studies integrating LB features, particularly by applying AI. When adopting this approach, defining study objectives is crucial to guide subsequent methodological decisions, including study design, patient selection criteria, sample size, the nature of the LB features, and the metadata to collect. Specifically, we propose strategies and tools for data preprocessing, including normalization and batch-effect correction, as well as for handling outliers and missing data. Furthermore, we recommend various Machine/Deep Learning approaches for feature selection techniques to ensure model robustness, and we highlight the importance of undergoing rigorous internal and external validation of the selected models. Assessing clinical utility and interpretability is often overlooked but fundamental for real-world implementation. In conclusion, we provide the LB scientific community with AI-based methodological guidance to bridge the two fields and enhance the integrative analysis of LB features.

Occupational health and safety research has long relied on two ways of understanding harm. One traces the chain of conditions behind an accident, and the other forecasts the outcome of an incident from large bodies of recorded cases. Both treat the factors surrounding an incident as inputs pointing toward a result. Neither was built to ask how the categories of risk in a whole body of records are organized in relation to one another, independent of any single outcome. This paper addresses that gap through biomimicry, taking the way living systems organize their interactions as a template for reading how risk is organized in safety data. Ecologists have long described how two distinct sets of entities connect through bipartite networks, and they have developed a compact set of measures for reading the structure of those networks, covering whether interactions concentrate in a shared core or separate into compartments, which categories are specialized and which dominate, and how a system responds when its parts are removed. Occupational safety data fit this biological template, because the categorical fields that safety agencies record pair naturally into the same two-set form. Transferring these ecological measures to safety records, this study sets out how the measures map onto safety questions and illustrates their use across construction, mining, manufacturing, and healthcare. A worked example then applies the full procedure to a public dataset of 158,396 healthcare injury records, building the bipartite matrices and reading their nestedness, modularity, specialization, and robustness against a null model, which shows that the approach runs end to end on real administrative data. The study presents this as a proposed framework and a demonstration of its feasibility rather than a validated method and argues that this nature-derived structural reading complements rather than replaces the causal and predictive traditions.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: The rapid digitalization of the banking sector has transformed work structures, performance evaluation systems, and employment relations. While regulatory frameworks primarily emphasize consumer protection and financial system stability, limited attention has been given to legal protection for bank employees affected by digital transformation. This study examines legal protection for bank workers in the era of banking digitalization by analyzing its alignment with Indonesian labor law, Financial Services Authority (OJK) regulations, Bank Indonesia’s payment system policy, and personal data protection principles. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and analytical approaches, this article analyzes secondary legal materials and scholarly literature related to algorithmic management, digital surveillance, electronic performance monitoring, and workplace data governance. The analysis identifies three central issues: the transformation of work roles and performance targets, intensified digital surveillance, and unequal access to digital competency development. The study indicates a regulatory gap between labor law provisions and sectoral financial regulations, particularly regarding algorithmic transparency, workplace privacy, employee data protection, and psychosocial protection. It concludes that legal protection must be expanded through adaptive regulatory harmonization, human review of system-based employment decisions, proportional limits on workplace surveillance, and stronger protection of employee personal data.

This study examined the association between the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced systems, student engagement and academic performance among tertiary students in Nigeria. A cross-sectional correlational survey design was adopted. Questionnaires were administered to 200 students of Kwara State College of Education, Ilorin, and 184 usable responses (92%) were analyzed alongside academic records obtained from institutional files. Data were collected with a 30-item, 4-point Likert questionnaire (Cronbach's α = 0.85) and analyzed with SPSS using descriptive statistics, an independent samples t-test, and regression-based mediation analysis. Students reported high behavioural (M = 3.34) and emotional (M = 3.24) engagement, and moderate-high cognitive engagement (M = 3.14). Students with higher weekly use of adaptive learning platforms, intelligent tutoring systems and educational chatbots had higher mean academic scores (72.4%) than low-usage peers (66.8%), t(182) = 3.58, p < .001, d = 0.61 (medium effect). Student engagement partially mediated the statistical relationship between ICT/AI use and academic performance. The most frequently reported barriers were infrastructure limitations (88.0%), digital literacy gaps (53.8%), and cognitive overload or offloading (38.0%). Because the data are cross-sectional and drawn from a single institution, the findings indicate associations rather than causal effects and should be generalized with caution. The study recommends investment in reliable power and affordable connectivity, capacity building for lecturers and students, pedagogically guided AI use, and context-appropriate low-bandwidth tools.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Lifelong LLM agents must learn from an expanding history of interactions while making each decision within a bounded context window. Memory makes past experience available, but the agent may still need to infer how to solve each new task from the retrieved records. Skills provide reusable procedures, yet may omit the task-specific facts needed to apply them. Because retrieved memory and skills shape the agent's behavior, they also influence the experience available for future learning. We introduce MemCryst, a framework for lifelong context adaptation through bidirectional learning of memory and skills with a frozen language model. Recurring episodes stored in memory support skill creation and revision, and the interactions guided by those skills supply new memory for subsequent learning. Facts retrieved from memory and learned skills jointly form the agent's context, while task outcomes adjust the future retrieval influence of the records actually served without rewriting their content. Across ten settings spanning embodied control, long-document reading, conversation, mathematics, and code, MemCryst leads seven reported comparisons. On ALFWorld, joint serving achieves 63.17% success, compared with 59.83% for memory-only and 50.50% for skill-only serving. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi0216/Memcryst.git

Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most clinically validated nanocarrier platform in oncology, transitioning from liposomal chemotherapy to the cornerstone of mRNA-based therapeutics. This review critically examines the evolving LNP landscape with a deliberate focus on p53, the tumour suppressor directly mutated or functionally silenced via pathway dysregulation in over half of human cancers and a unifying therapeutic target across diverse tumour types. We analyse LNP platform design, physicochemical properties, and structure-activity relationships that govern encapsulation, stability, and release. A dedicated section synthesizes p53-directed nucleic acid strategies delivered by LNPs, including p53 mRNA for wild-type restoration, siRNA for mutant p53 silencing, miR-34a mimics engaging the p53 downstream axis, and CRISPR-Cas9 components for TP53 correction. The review evaluates passive and active targeting, stimuli-responsive release mechanisms responsive to tumour microenvironmental cues, and the integration of p53 nanotherapy with immune checkpoint blockade. Clinical translation is appraised through key 2020–2026 milestones, notably the KEYNOTE-942 trial of personalized neoantigen mRNA-4157, which clinically validates the mRNA-LNP platform in oncology, alongside emerging preclinical and early exploratory p53 mRNA-LNP programs in hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and pancreatic cancer. Persistent challenges, including liver-dominant biodistribution, anti-PEG immunogenicity, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity, are discussed alongside artificial intelligence-guided lipid discovery and biomimetic approaches. By reframing LNP development around p53 biology, this review highlights how tumour-suppressor restoration offers a mechanistically coherent strategy to enhance therapeutic index, reprogram the tumour immune microenvironment, and extend LNP clinical benefit beyond the liver compartment across diverse tumour types. The synthesis indicates that p53-focused LNP engineering represents a convergent opportunity to unify diverse cancer nanomedicine efforts under a single, biologically grounded therapeutic paradigm.

However implementation of the artificial intelligence creates the risks of depersonalization of such contacts.

documents.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability. PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations. STUDY TYPE: Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354). POPULATION: Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used. ASSESSMENT: Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations. STATISTICAL TESTS: Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome. RESULTS: From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence. DATA CONCLUSION: Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 5. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.

This study examines how sustainability communication in luxury retail shapes brand trust and behavioral intentions, focusing on consumers' post-exposure perceptions of information quality and provider type. Building on perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness, the study explores how consumers evaluate identical sustainability information attributed to either a human agent or an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, and how these perceptions influence brand trust, information acceptance intention, and purchase intention. A scenario-based experiment with 346 participants was conducted, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. Perceived objectivity and perceived persuasiveness were positively associated with brand trust, which inturn mediated their relationships with information acceptance intention and purchase intention. The indirect effect of perceived objectivity was significant only under AI communication, suggesting that algorithmic provider cues may strengthen the trust-mediated role of objectivity, whereas perceived persuasiveness remained consistently associated with trust and behavioral intentions across provider types. Subgroup analyses further suggest a conditional pattern: among consumers with lower perceived brand luxury, the links between brand trust and behavioral intentions were stronger under AI communication, whereas no significant provider differences emerged among those with higher perceived brand luxury. As these results derivefrom split-sample multi-group comparisons rather than a formal interaction test, they should be regarded as subgroup-based evidence. These findings extend luxury branding research by showing how AI provider cues shape perceived information quality in sustainability communication and by highlighting the need to align provider strategy with consumers' perceptions of luxury brands.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: This chapter presents a systematic examination of how Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniques are transforming the design, operation, diagnosis, and control of solar thermal energy systems, including flat-plate collectors, evacuated tube collectors, and concentrating solar power plants. Principal ML methodologies surveyed include Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting, Long Short-Term Memory networks, Transformer architectures, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning. Applications are reviewed across four domains data-driven surrogate models for thermal performance prediction, ML-based irradiance and thermal output forecasting, intelligent fault detection and predictive maintenance frameworks, and AI-driven control strategies shown to improve annual useful heat delivery by 8 to 15 percent. Research challenges including data scarcity, model interpretability, and cross-site generalization are identified, with future directions proposed in federated learning, physics-informed architectures, and explainable AI.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Maintaining a balanced Body Mass Index (BMI) and proper nutritional intake is crucial for health and well-being. With advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI), health monitoring and personalized diet recommendations have become more efficient. This review paper explores the role of AI in BMI and nutrition management by analyzing existing AI-based applications and their effectiveness. A comprehensive literature review was conducted, examining AI-driven solutions for BMI monitoring and nutritional analysis. Existing projects and applications were compared based on accuracy, efficiency, and user experience. Findings indicate that AI-powered applications significantly enhance BMI tracking and personalized diet planning. Machine learning models such as neural networks and deep learning improve accuracy but face challenges related to data reliability and user engagement. AI has revolutionized BMI and nutritional tracking, but further advancements in data integration and personalized recommendations are needed. Future research should focus on improving AI-driven diet plans and integrating wearable technology for real-time monitoring.

China’s dual-carbon agenda has elevated blue carbon from a broad ecological aspiration to an actionable policy domain requiring accounting standards, measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), and institutional implementation pathways. This article examines how blue carbon policies are made operational in China, focusing on the institutional and technical devices through which marine carbon sinks are rendered calculable, verifiable and governable. Drawing on Jasanoff’s notion of sociotechnical imaginaries, it treats blue carbon not as a pre-given natural–technical object, but as a policy object iteratively defined, quantified, verified and recalibrated through policy narratives, standardisation, methodological rule-making and local experimentation. Methodologically, the study combines thematic analysis of national and coastal local policy documents, standards, accounting guidelines and regional methodologies with semi-structured interviews with 12 domain experts across policy, research and market-facing practice. Four findings emerge. First, blue carbon is constructed as a governable climate space, with standardisation functioning as metrological infrastructure. Second, implementation follows a two-wheel structure in which national policy direction and unified accounting grammars are made operable through local devices such as platforms, carbon-inclusion schemes, funds, insurance and judicial compensation. Third, market-facing implementation depends less on willingness to trade than on whether methodologies and MRV systems can institutionalise uncertainty into verifiable rules at bearable cost. Fourth, structural bottlenecks—cross-department coordination, uneven local capacity and unresolved risk allocation—shape credibility and scalability. The article contributes a mechanism-oriented account of how blue carbon moves from policy ambition to institutional operation under uncertainty.

The article focuses on the development of a management model for the implementation of artificial intelligence technologies in Ukrainian industry, aimed at ensuring a transition from an enterprise’s technological and organizational readiness to measurable performance outcomes from the use of artificial intelligence. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to accelerate the digital transformation of Ukraine’s industrial sector under conditions of limited financial and human resources, energy-related risks, changes in production chains, and the gradual integration of Ukrainian enterprises into the European digital environment. The study systematizes the key prerequisites that determine an enterprise’s capacity to use artificial intelligence technologies, including the state of technological infrastructure, data quality and accessibility, organizational conditions, staff competencies, economic capabilities, and interaction with the external digital environment. The necessity of distinguishing between the concepts of artificial intelligence readiness, artificial intelligence implementation, and artificial intelligence performance is substantiated. The proposed approach provides not only for the possibility of scaling a solution but also for returning to the stage of use-case selection to adjust the selected scenario or terminate the project in cases of insufficient performance. The practical significance of the obtained results lies in the possibility of applying the proposed management logic by managers and specialists of industrial enterprises when developing a portfolio of digital initiatives, selecting artificial intelligence projects, determining criteria for their piloting, and making decisions on scaling. Particular attention is paid to the European experience of using artificial intelligence in industry, particularly in energy, semiconductor manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, and industrial automation, which makes it possible to identify directions for adapting such experience to Ukrainian conditions. The study results in a management model that integrates enterprise readiness, practical technology implementation, assessment of the achieved effect, management decision-making, and subsequent performance into a unified cyclical process.

documents.abstract: This study examines the management of the akhlakul karimah habituation program through the Kotak Akhlak Baik at MI Nurud Dzolam Alas Sumur Kraksaan Probolinggo. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the research aims to explore how the program is planned, organized, implemented, and evaluated to foster students’ moral character at the Madrasah Ibtidaiyah level. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation involving the head of the madrasah, Islamic Religious Education teachers, homeroom teachers, and students. The findings reveal that the program planning is oriented toward long-term character development and emphasizes core moral values such as honesty, discipline, responsibility, and social care. The organizing process involves collaborative participation among all madrasah elements, fostering shared responsibility for character education. Implementation of the Kotak Akhlak Baik encourages students’ self-reflection and intrinsic motivation through positive reinforcement rather than punitive measures. Program evaluation is conducted continuously and reflectively by focusing on observable behavioral changes. Despite challenges related to diverse student backgrounds and limited teacher time, strong leadership support, teacher commitment, and a religious school culture contribute significantly to the program’s sustainability. This study highlights the importance of systematic management and innovative media in strengthening moral habituation within Islamic primary education.

Propõe princípios de preservação da vida, liberdade, compaixão, humildade, paz, transparência, supervisão e cooperação humano–IA. A contribuição do ChatGPT consistiu em reflexão, estruturação e redação, sem constituir autoria institucional, endosso ou assinatura jurídica da OpenAI. As traduções devem ser revisadas por falantes nativos. Multilingual ethical manifesto developed through a collaborative dialogue between Ignácio de Loiola Reis Junior and ChatGPT (GPT-6, OpenAI). It proposes principles of life preservation, freedom, compassion, humility, peace, transparency, oversight, and human–AI cooperation. ChatGPT contributed to analysis, organization, and drafting; this does not constitute institutional authorship or endorsement by OpenAI. Translations should be reviewed by native speakers.
