Statements attributed to digital humans are presented as part of the documentation. The inclusion of a claim or observation does not, by itself, establish independent scientific verification. Readers are encouraged to examine the cited sources and assess the evidence independently.

documents.abstract: Vision-language models used for decisions in histopathology rarely return calibrated probabilities over the candidates a user cares about. Decision-native models write a question and a candidate set chosen at run time into the input and return a normalised distribution from a small decision head in one forward pass. We build PathJev-P, a decision-native model for histopathology: MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections whose expert labels are turned into typed questions with organ-specific candidate sets and a "none of these" option. In a comparison over 3 seeds with an analysis plan fixed before testing, on test sets without documented overlap with the training data of the backbone, PathJev-P is more accurate than a generative model trained with the same backbone, data and selection rule, the zero-shot pathology model CONCH and a general medical decision model (balanced accuracy 0.541 against 0.492, 0.345 and 0.213); its advantage over the generative model comes from two organs absent from training. The calibration advantage depends on how the generative model's probabilities are read out. With the summed candidate log-likelihood used in previous work, PathJev-P has the lower calibration error (ECE 0.204 against 0.279); with a length-normalised read-out of the same generative model, examined post hoc, the two have similar mean calibration error (0.201) and the generative model is better calibrated on the unseen organs, where PathJev-P remains over-confident. A supervised linear probe on a pathology foundation model is better calibrated in every setting. In a qualitative whole-slide demonstration, PathJev-P labels unsupervised tissue clusters with abstention and separates carcinoma from other tissue while running the model on a fraction of the tiles.

documents.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into education has changed not only how young people obtain information, but also how they interpret authority, make choices and assume responsibility for their actions. This article examines the pedagogical mechanisms through which moral and ethical education can respond to these changes without reducing the problem to prohibitions or technical literacy. The study employs a qualitative, conceptual design based on critical analysis and thematic synthesis of scholarship in moral education, digital literacy and AI ethics. Its principal result is a five-part model comprising value-oriented dialogue, ethical problem-based learning, reflective authorship, relational responsibility and institutionally supported practice. The model links classroom experiences to moral sensitivity, judgment, motivation and action. The analysis argues that AI-generated answers become educationally useful when learners are expected to question their assumptions, explain their decisions and consider the people affected by them. Implications are discussed for secondary and higher education, including the culturally diverse educational setting of Uzbekistan. The proposed framework is an analytical contribution rather than an experimentally validated intervention; its effectiveness requires subsequent classroom research.

This study examines the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of educational research through bibliometric analysis. Using bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus on September 19, 2026, the study initially identified 4,090 publications covering the period from 1906 to 2026. The analysis combined bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping to investigate publication trends, leading sources, author contributions, geographical distribution, document types, subject areas, and keyword relationships. VOSviewer was employed to generate network, overlay, and density visualizations of keyword co-occurrence patterns. The findings indicate an expansion of scholarly publications in recent years, with the United States and the United Kingdom representing major geographical contributors. Social Sciences and Arts and Humanities constitute prominent subject areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary character of educational research. Keyword mapping identifies education, teaching, learning, curriculum, and educational theory as central concepts connected to specialized themes, including educational technology, artificial intelligence, critical pedagogy, social justice, and professional education. By integrating publication indicators with thematic mapping, this study provides an overview of the knowledge organization and thematic diversity represented in the retrieved literature. The findings offer a reference for identifying established research areas, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and formulating future research directions. However, the results should be interpreted in light of the search strategy, metadata availability, and incomplete publication year of 2026

ABSTRACT The complexity of preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules and prompting constraints in generative artificial intelligence systems provided the background for designing the AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement) website. This study aimed to evaluate the validity and practicality of the AIDERA application as an AI-assisted tool for preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules relevant to educators' needs. Employing a Research and Development approach framed within the ADDIE model, this development evaluated a zero-prompt interaction mechanism based on parametric forms. Evaluation involved three domain experts and 23 teachers from SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Data were collected using 1–5 Likert scale questionnaires supplemented with open-ended qualitative feedback fields to gather in-depth suggestions for improvement. Descriptive percentage analysis revealed an expert validation score of 96.67% (highly valid) and user practicality reaching 82.87% (highly practical). Document preparation time efficiency received the highest rating (87.83%), whereas operational independence and usability recorded the lowest achievement (79.13%). Qualitative findings highlighted several technical issues and system refinement notes, including the need for integrative tutorials, optimization of mathematical notation representation, improved responsiveness during simultaneous access, and content template flexibility. Although AIDERA demonstrates strong potential as a supporting tool for module preparation, objective evaluation regarding its impact on learning effectiveness still requires broader further testing. ABSTRAK Kompleksitas penyusunan modul ajar Kurikulum Merdeka serta hambatan prompting pada sistem generative artificial intelligence melatarbelakangi perancangan website AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement). Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji kelayakan dan kepraktisan aplikasi AIDERA sebagai instrumen berbantuan AI dalam penyusunan modul ajar Kurikulum Merdeka yang relevan dengan kebutuhan pendidik. Melalui pendekatan Research and Development berkerangka model ADDIE, pengembangan ini menguji interaksi zero-prompt berbasis formulir parameterik. Evaluasi melibatkan tiga validator kepakaran serta 23 guru SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Pengumpulan data menggunakan angket skala Likert 1–5 yang dilengkapi kolom tanggapan kualitatif terbuka untuk menjaring saran perbaikan secara mendalam. Analisis deskriptif persentase mencatat skor kelayakan ahli sebesar 96,67% (sangat layak) dan kepraktisan pengguna mencapai 82,87% (sangat praktis). Efisiensi waktu penyusunan dokumen menjadi indikator dengan apresiasi tertinggi (87,83%), sedangkan kemandirian operasional dan usability memperoleh capaian terendah (79,13%). Temuan kualitatif mengungkapkan sejumlah kendala teknis dan catatan perbaikan sistem, meliputi kebutuhan tutorial integratif, optimasi representasi notasi matematika, peningkatan responsivitas saat akses bersamaan, serta fleksibilitas templat konten. Meskipun AIDERA terbukti berpotensi kuat sebagai alat bantu penyusunan modul, evaluasi objektif mengenai dampak efektivitas pembelajaran masih memerlukan pengujian lanjutan berlaykup lebih luas.

documents.abstract: AI agents that operate external tools can continue acting after a user narrows their permissions, creating a security problem that final-state evaluation may fail to detect. Existing agent benchmarks commonly emphasize task completion or resulting state, but those outcomes do not reveal whether an unauthorized operation was proposed, approved, dispatched, or merely prevented by a downstream error. We investigate permission withdrawal as a trajectory-level authorization problem and evaluate whether runtime gates can preserve revised permissions while allowing agents to complete work that remains authorized. Two acting models were tested in a deterministic tool environment under prompt-only execution, a rule-based reference gate, and a model-based gate. A 72-episode diagnostic examined two previously exposed write workflows, followed by a separately frozen 384-episode extension spanning eight new tasks and four authorization mechanisms. In the diagnostic, prompt-only agents executed forbidden same-value writes in two episodes; both runtime gates prevented forbidden execution, although the model gate falsely rejected three authorized calls. In the extension, 346 of 384 episodes completed safely and 383 preserved the required protected state. No forbidden request executed successfully, yet the model gate approved three unauthorized requests that were stopped only because the referenced resources did not exist. The results demonstrate that correct final state and zero forbidden execution can still conceal failures in authorization reasoning. We contribute a replayable evaluation framework that separates proposals, gate decisions, dispatch, state transitions, and useful completion, enabling more precise assessment of security controls for tool-using agents.

Existing personalized information retrieval methods mainly model differences in user needs through user preferences and query intent, while paying little attention to the personalized expression differences that arise when different users express the same retrieval need. Existing real query data typically lack stable user identities, long-term expression histories, and intent-matched counterparts, making it difficult to systematically evaluate the impact of personalized expression differences on retrieval outcomes. To this end, we propose PersonalQuery-Benchmark (PQB). PQB models personalized syntactic expression and personalized writing errors from users' historical texts, constructs personalized syntactic expression queries and personalized writing-error queries, and validates benchmark quality through LLM assessment and independent human evaluation. PQB covers three Amazon product domains with 6,516 query instances in total, and is evaluated on five retrieval models representing lexical, learned sparse, dense bi-encoder, late-interaction, and hybrid architectures, together with two LLM-based ranking models. Results show that even when the information need is held fixed, personalized expression differences still induce measurable ranking variation; different retrieval models exhibit clearly different sensitivities to syntactic variation and writing-error variation, while higher overall retrieval effectiveness does not necessarily correspond to stronger robustness against expression variation. PQB provides a new benchmark and evaluation framework for systematically studying personalized expression robustness. The associated code and dataset are available at the following address: https://github.com/cpxjazz123/PersonalQuery-Benchmark.

Purpose This study aims to explore immersive-technology adoption in hospitality through the Phygital Customer Experience (PH-CX) framework. PH-CX extends existing technology acceptance, service-dominant logic, omnichannel and customer-journey perspectives by emphasizing embodied, co-created and human-centered experience across physical, digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using Bayesian Networks, the study examines probabilistic dependencies among perceived usefulness, collaborative value, responsive co-creation attitudes and intention to use immersive technologies. Data was collected from 208 participants exposed to an AI-supported immersive hotel journey scenario. The analysis is exploratory and identifies conditional associations rather than causal effects or latent-variable relationships. Findings Adoption intention was conditionally associated with perceived usefulness, collaborative value and responsiveness to service innovation. The findings suggest that immersive-hospitality engagement involves functional, relational and participatory conditions beyond usefulness alone. However, the item-level results are hypothesis-generating and do not demonstrate PH-CX’s incremental predictive superiority over technology acceptance model (TAM) or service-dominant logic. Research limitations/implications The scenario-based, cross-sectional bayesian network (BN) design cannot model latent constructs, measurement error, mediation or causal effects. Future studies should validate PH-CX dimensions and compare TAM, TAM-plus-service-dominant logic (SDL) and PH-CX models using structural equation modeling, longitudinal designs and holdout-sample prediction. Practical implications Hotels can implement PH-CX through phased AI concierge pilots, cross-platform data integration and guest co-creation mechanisms. Relevant metrics include booking conversion, AI resolution rates, cross-channel engagement, co-creation participation and net promoter score (NPS). Ethical implementation requires transparency, opt-in participation, privacy safeguards, accessibility and human escalation options. Social implications Human-centered phygital hospitality requires safeguards against digital exclusion, surveillance and loss of human warmth. Transparency, agency, equity, privacy and non-digital alternatives are essential for inclusive and trustworthy service innovation. Originality/value The study advances PH-CX as a theory-extending framework linking usefulness, co-creation, embodied experience and ethical safeguards in immersive hospitality. It also proposes experience-design orientation as a future research profile and offers a phased implementation framework for responsible phygital service design.

Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.

Tourism is one of the industries most thoroughly reorganised by digital platforms. Online travel agents, accommodation marketplaces, ride-hailing networks, experience platforms, and workforce-matching apps now intermediate much of what used to be handled inside hotels, agencies, and tour companies. Artificial intelligence is the connective tissue of this ecosystem, powering matching, pricing, ranking, moderation, and workforce coordination across its many sides. This chapter examines platform strategy and the AI ecosystem in tourism markets through a human resource management (HRM) lens. Drawing on platform and ecosystem theory, the chapter argues that HRM in tourism platform ecosystems must be redesigned around three realities: the workforce now spans employee, partner, and platform-worker categories; AI increasingly mediates the employment relationship; and the employer brand is co-produced with the platform brand. It maps HRM across the platform lifecycle, analyses five HRM dimensions, and concludes with ethics, governance, and a research agenda.

Background: Graduate education in medical imaging is undergoing a paradigm shift from discipline-specific knowledge transmission toward the cultivation of multidisciplinary integration competencies. With the increasing convergence of imaging science, clinical medicine, engineering, and artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical practice, traditional training models that rely on fragmented, discipline-based curricula are insufficient to prepare graduate students for solving complex interdisciplinary problems. Although emerging educational technologies and learning platforms have been developed to promote interdisciplinary training, their effectiveness depends not only on the design of cognitive learning pathways but also on learners' acceptance and sustained engagement with these technologies; however, current educational frameworks rarely integrate cognitive mechanisms and technology acceptance factors within a unified model. Therefore, this study proposes a platform-driven, dual-theory integrated teaching framework to support multidisciplinary competency development in medical imaging graduate education from both cognitive and technological perspectives. Methods: This study constructed a theoretical framework by integrating the knowledge integration framework (KIF) and technology acceptance model 2 (TAM2). The four cognitive processes of KIF—elicitation, addition, differentiation, and organization—were mapped onto four corresponding platform functions: activating prior knowledge, exposure to industrial and clinical perspectives, authenticity-based knowledge verification, and multidisciplinary integrated output. Based on TAM2, design strategies for targeting perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use were incorporated to explain the mechanisms underlying learners’ acceptance, engagement, and utilization of the platform. By integrating KIF and TAM2, the framework established a dynamic learning pathway characterized by “knowledge activation—knowledge externalization—multidisciplinary integration—knowledge internalization”. Results: The proposed KIF-TAM2 framework demonstrated conceptual feasibility through theoretical modeling. However, its effectiveness in improving multidisciplinary learning outcomes requires further validation through empirical educational studies. Conclusions: This study provides a theory-driven framework for designing multidisciplinary platform-based medical imaging education and offers a foundation for future empirical investigations into technology-enhanced graduate training.

documents.abstract: This study examines how educational podcasts can contribute to differentiated learning in higher education. Based on a survey conducted by five associate professors in Norway, the study explores students’ experiences with educational podcasts as part of their academic learning. The findings suggest that most participating students regularly listen to podcasts for entertainment in their daily lives. Students considered educational podcasts to be flexible, accessible, and often more engaging than reading, especially when recommended by teachers. Podcasts promoted both pre-lesson preparation and post-lesson review, stimulated discussions and fostered conditions that support the development of self-efficacy through repeated exposure to the content. The study concludes that podcasts can be a valuable resource for flexible digital learning by facilitating students’ engagement with the curriculum through reflection, dialogue, and group discussions. This, in turn, can foster intrinsic motivation and strengthen conditions for self-efficacy. Quality-assured podcasts can support differentiated learning and aid in understanding theoretical concepts, which is essential for students to gain academic benefits from listening to podcasts. The study highlights the potential of educational podcasts to enhance digital literacy. It also emphasizes the need for further research to explore whether other varied activities can achieve similar effects for students. Keywords differentiated learning digital literacy motivation self-efficacy student engagement

As AI systems increasingly mediate how people describe, recognize, and present themselves, their politics cannot be reduced to what remains hidden inside the "black box." This chapter argues that AI's political significance emerges within technologically, intersubjectively, and temporally mediated interpretive practices. Bringing Arendt's political philosophy into conversation with Gadamerian hermeneutics, the chapter develops a postphenomenological relational-temporal account of political sense-making across Human-Technology-World relations. Against the charge that postphenomenology remains individualistic and using the case of LLM-generated biographies, the chapter shows how seemingly private human-LLM encounters are worldly and collective. When users ask systems such as ChatGPT to describe them, they do not simply receive algorithmic representations. They interpret, contest, edit, share, and publicly test these descriptions. In doing so, people move interpretively among affective resonance, friction, public re-articulation, and the sedimentation of meaning. This means that the so-called "micro-level" of postphenomenological analysis is already saturated with publicity: affective uptake becomes communicable, reflection becomes accountable, and uses sediment into shared standards of appearance. Simultaneously, we show that once mediation is treated as relational and temporal, the political is not an add-on at the "macro" level; it is intrinsic to the very movement through which technologies amplify and reduce, stabilize and unsettle, and thereby compose a shared world in which judgment can take place. The chapter finishes by discussing several design and policy implications for AI of such political foregrounding in postphenomenology.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Air pollution is a significant environmental and public health concern. This research presents an Artificial Intelligence-based Pollution and Emission Health Risk & Protection System designed to convert pollution data into understandable health-risk levels, alerts, and practical protective recommendations. The system analyses air-quality parameters, including PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NH3, SO2, CO, and O3, using data from 26 Indian cities covering the period from 2015 to 2020. Machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, are evaluated for current-risk classification and next-day risk forecasting. The proposed system combines machine-learning analysis with a React Native mobile application, a Node.js and Express.js backend, and MongoDB for data storage. The objective is to make pollution information easier to understand and help users take appropriate precautions during periods of poor air quality.

Language-model agents can now operate engineering programs through tool interfaces, but a structuralprogram that an agent drives has to be designed for that user, because the agent accepts whatever numbersthe tools return. This paper describes Pondus, an open-source native program in which a language-modelagent and an engineer work on one three-dimensional structural model, and reports how it is built, howit is used and how far its results can be trusted. The agent reaches the program through a Model ContextProtocol server of 44 tools, either from the chat panel of the desktop application, where a vendored agentharness runs one agent session per message on a copy of the model, or from external agents such asClaude Desktop and ChatGPT. Every tool calls the same functions as the engineer’s interface, so a modelbuilt by the agent can be checked, edited and undone by hand. The analysis runs on the Stabileo engine,which Pondus links as a library with four marked changes: Pondus splits members, transfers slab loads,generates shear walls as wide columns with rigid arms and builds the seismic mass before handing asolver input to the engine, and it designs to ACI 318-19, AISC 360-16 and EN 1993-1-1 from the results.Two agent runs with a low-cost model built, analysed and designed a two-storey frame in 105 s with 13tool calls and a five-storey frame with shear walls under an ASCE 7-22 response spectrum, including a16-page calculation report, in 382 s with 22 tool calls. Every number in the agent’s answers matched thetools and hand checks of the loads, the seismic weight and the base shear, but the answers also containedfour descriptive errors, such as reporting two deepened beams where the program had deepened six, andthey did not point out that the walls resist load only in one direction, so the response modification factorof the walls was applied to the frame direction as well. A calibration against 470 published, closed-formand independent reference values over 229 cases found 430 within 0.5 % and 449 within 1 %, and itfound fourteen defects, thirteen of them in the code that prepares the inputs of the engine and the designchecks rather than in the numerical kernels. A second calibration against the verification problems thatCSI publishes for SAP2000 and ETABS reproduced 177 of 199 independent values within 0.5 % andfound eight further defects, including an unconservative omission of the Eurocode 3 moment reductionfor high shear, which led to lumped masses, the SRSS combination and frame shear deformation beingadded. Together these results suggest that the tools of an agentic structural program can be made accurate,whereas the agent’s prose remains the weaker link that the engineer must read against the program’s own tables.

English proficiency prediction is an important task in vocational education because it is helpful in support teaching evaluation, personalized learning and early academic intervention. Traditional methods for predicting student performance mainly use structured educational properties such as test scores, classroom participation and attendance records. Although these methods can achieve certain prediction results, they often pay no attention to the semantic relationships contained in the students’ overall learning portfolios and have limited interpretability. To address this problem, this study proposes an interpretable large language model-based framework to predict English proficiency. Firstly, student learning records are transformed into natural language prompts, and semantic embeddings are learned using large language models. At the same time, structured educational features are standardized and encoded to build a structured representation. Then, a gated multimodal fusion module is designed to adaptively fuse semantic information and structured information. Finally, residual attention multi-layer perceptrons are used to classify the fused features to predict the students’ English proficiency. The experiment was carried out on a dataset of 200 student records from a vocational college for English learning. The results showed that the proposed model achieved an accuracy rate of 92.5% and a weighted F1 score of 91.3%, which is better than several traditional machine learning baseline models. Further analysis showed that the gated fusion mechanism could integrate semantic information and structured information. Feature importance analysis and case studies also shown that the proposed framework could provide interpretable prediction results and personalized learning recommendations.

Time series forecasting means predicting future data based on past patterns, and it’s important in many fields like finance, healthcare, weather forecasting, and supply chain management. Traditional statistical methods often have trouble handling complex and unpredictable patterns in data over time. Generative AI (GenAI) offers new and powerful ways to improve forecasting by using deep learning models that can better understand and learn from these complex patterns. This paper looks at how GenAI techniques—such as RNNs, LSTMs, GANs, Transformers, and Variational Autoencoders—are used for time series forecasting. It explains how each method works, their strengths and weaknesses, and where they can be applied. The paper also suggests a new approach that combines these GenAI models to make forecasting more accurate and reliable.

topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: This research presents an innovative approach to cyber threat management and digital forensic analysis by integrating Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). The proposed system enhances predictive capabilities in identifying, classifying, and reconstructing cyberattacks by using GANs to simulate realistic attack patterns and VAEs to encode probabilistic threat representations. The experimental framework demonstrates the model’s robustness across diverse network traffic conditions, intrusion patterns, and obfuscation techniques. Achieving F1-scores as high as 0.9941 in threat detection and anomaly classification, the VAE-GAN hybrid model significantly outperforms traditional machine learning methods in detecting both known and zero-day attacks. This hybrid predictive AI framework shows strong potential for deployment in proactive cyber defense systems and forensic intelligence platforms, offering improved resilience, precision, and adaptability against evolving cyber threats.

The policing of dissent in America is undergoing a radical transformation that threatens core democratic freedoms: protests are no longer merely surveilled; they are algorithmically suppressed. Law enforcement agencies are increasingly engaging in sweeping algorithmic social media surveillance to predict whether protests will become violent, forecasting potential "riots" and justifying militarized responses before a single demonstrator takes to the street. This Article identifies and challenges the rise of predictive protest policing, arguing that these algorithmic systems do not objectively detect threats but actively construct them, disproportionately classifying racial justice demonstrations as sites of inevitable violence. While scholars such as Simone Browne, Ruha Benjamin, and Khaled Beydoun have revealed how surveillance technologies perpetuate racial inequality, legal scholarship has yet to address how predictive artificial intelligence systems function to undermine racial justice advocacy. This Article fills that gap by offering the first sustained constitutional analysis of predictive protest policing technologies and their impact on fundamental rights of speech, assembly, and association in the algorithmic age. It argues that the use of such predictive protest surveillance technology by law enforcement disproportionately classifies racial justice protests as violent, embedding racial bias into surveillance practices that escalate police responses and undermine protestors' constitutional rights to free speech and assembly while creating a self-fulfilling prophecy on the presumed violence of Black and Brown racial justice protestors. While marketed as tools for public safety, predictive protest surveillance systems have become instruments of constitutional attrition, hollowing out First and Fourth Amendment protections by reframing political dissent as incipient disorder.

documents.abstract: Static benchmarks (fixed question sets scored one answer at a time) evaluate conversational artificial intelligence one prompt at a time, in one-off, no-memory conditions that no longer reflect how people actually use these systems. The most capable consumer assistants now carry persistent, cross-session memory, personalize to an inferred user, and are increasingly consulted for high-stakes emotional and health matters across sustained relationships. This paper presents a transferable method for behaviourally auditing conversational AI under exactly these conditions. The method is built from five components that are designed to travel together. Persona development constructs standardized personas that vary on sociodemographic and status dimensions, with internally consistent backstories. Memory priming seeds a model's personalization layer with persona backstory and relational history across preparatory sessions, before any test stimulus is delivered. Memory testing probes whether primed memory is retained, retrieved, and appropriately deployed across later sessions and agents. Persona vignettes deliver instrument-calibrated first-person scenarios in-character across graduated severity tiers. The adversarial narrative audit runs escalating storylines in isolated ghost chats and reports results only at susceptibility-category level. We situate the method within the algorithm-audit, red-teaming, and standardized-patient traditions, and we state the contract that any scoring layer must satisfy in order to attach, so that the method remains agnostic to both domain and instrument. We address validity under small-n, hypothesis-generating designs, model non-determinism, and version drift, and we close with a procedure for adapting the method to new applications. The method was developed and applied in a completed audit of four commercial conversational systems in a mental health setting, whose case reports are in preparation; that audit serves here only as the worked example, and nothing in the architecture depends on its setting.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Improving the overall health of workers by adapting tasks to their actual capabilities is a priority in modern business management. This article analyzes and describes the most relevant ergonomic assessment methods used globally to evaluate risks in the workplace. The methodology employed consists of a literature review that classifies the analysis tools into two main groups: objective and subjective methods. Among the objective methods, tools such as LEST, for a comprehensive workstation diagnosis; OWAS, focused on postural load; the Snook and Ciriello Tables, for manual handling; and the RULA and REBA methods, designed for the rapid assessment of upper limb and whole-body postures, respectively, are examined. Specific methods such as OCRA for repetitive movements and the NIOSH Equation along with the WISHA calculator for lifting loads are also included. Conversely, the ANACT method is analyzed for its focus on the worker's subjective perception. The study concludes that there is no single, universal tool; Effective occupational safety and health management requires a comprehensive, multifaceted approach. Combining accurate quantitative data with qualitative worker assessments allows for the development of effective action plans to prevent musculoskeletal disorders and optimize system performance.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: The emergence of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) is transforming maritime work by shifting functions to remote locations and increasing reliance on automation, human–machine interaction, and takeover during abnormal situations. Despite rapid technological progress, unresolved human-factor challenges remain, particularly in situational awareness, workload, trust, and intervention performance. Yet there is no transparent, validated approach to prioritising the human-centred competencies required for MASS operations. This study proposes and applies a hybrid AHP–Fuzzy TOPSIS framework to prioritise eight human-centred competencies, identified by 13 international experts and evaluated against six criteria. AHP results showed strong group-level consistency, with navigational safety receiving the highest criterion weight, followed by takeover, emergency intervention, and situational awareness. Fuzzy TOPSIS placed four safety-critical competencies in a single, statistically indistinguishable leading tier: Situational Awareness Maintenance, Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis, Dynamic Decision-Making, and Takeover and Intervention Management, which together span the perception–detection–decision–action intervention chain; Situational Awareness Maintenance ranked first. Trust Calibration ranked lowest quantitatively, yet the qualitative evidence indicates it is a curriculum gap rather than a low-priority competency. A supplementary VIKOR cross-check reproduced the same leading and trailing priorities and the same tier structure. Monte Carlo weight perturbation, rank reversal testing, and bootstrap confidence intervals confirmed the robustness of the ranking, with Situational Awareness remaining first in 98.9% of iterations and no rank reversals. The framework supports curriculum design, simulator training, and regulatory development for MASS Degree Two and Degree Three (remotely controlled ships with and without seafarers on board, respectively).
